blocks.text: `phase1_test_drive` drives the robot with the simulated RC transmitter from a simple plan, then prints a summary, shows a results figure and plays a bird's-eye replay. It switches the transmitter on, arms the robot and puts it in MANUAL mode automatically.

A plan is an N x 3 matrix `[t v w]`: from time `t` [s], hold forward speed `v` [m/s] and yaw rate `w` [rad/s] until the next row. Positive `v` is forward, positive `w` is a **left** turn. Limits: |v| <= 2.0 m/s and |w| <= 1.0 rad/s (larger values are clipped).

res = phase1_test_drive();                                  % default demo
plan = [0 0 0;  4 1.0 0;  15 1.0 0.4;  25 0 0];
res = phase1_test_drive('Plan', plan);                      % your own drive
res = phase1_test_drive('EStopAt', 20, 'ResetAt', 25);      % remote E-stop, then reset
res = phase1_test_drive('RCLoss', [20 23]);                 % radio link lost 20-23 s
res = phase1_test_drive('Implement', 1);                    % with the mower (2 tiller, 3 sprayer)
res = phase1_test_drive('Plan', plan, 'StopTime', 40, 'Replay', false);
For the E-stop and RC-loss options the script also performs the operator recovery: it centres the sticks, presses reset and cycles the arm switch, so the plan resumes afterwards.

The printed summary gives the MCU mode sequence (expected: BOOT -> SELFTEST -> STANDBY -> MANUAL at about 2 s), the distance and maximum speed, the battery use, the SBUS frame counts (rejected frames should be 0) and collisions. The figure ({fig:F23_d1_dashboard.png}) shows command vs actual speed and yaw rate, the path, the left/right track speeds, and the battery current with the MCU mode.

blocks.caption: Results figure of the default demo: speed and yaw rate follow the RC commands within about 0.02 m/s and 0.01 rad/s; 34.8 m driven, 0 rejected SBUS frames.

blocks.text: The run log is saved in `work/results/D1_<date>_<time>.mat` (path in `res.file`). The default 64 s drive takes about 4-6 min, because the simulation runs at about 0.3-0.5 times real time.
